subject: Cross-border data flow: hospital network transfer impact assessment

Subject: Request: Cross-border data flow assessment for EU Hospitals Network

Hi Kimberly,

We're working on procurement for the EU Hospitals Network and need a Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA) / cross-border data flow statement from Redwood to satisfy our Data Protection Officer and our procurement team. Specifically we need:
- Confirmation of where patient data and metadata may be processed (region/hypervisor level).
- Whether any patient-level or pseudonymised records could be routed to non-EU infrastructure under normal operations or failover.
- Details on KV cache behavior, backups, and any replication to offsite regions.
- The standard DPA + SCCs you propose and any additional contractual safeguards (e.g., DPIA support).

I've attached our standard template to fill (EU-Hospitals_TIA_template.xlsx). Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide a short, signable statement for procurement, and whether a brief technical walkthrough (30 min) with your security/privacy leads is possible next week?

Thanks,
Emma Jensen
Procurement Manager
EU Hospitals Network

Subject: Re: Request: Cross-border data flow assessment for EU Hospitals Network

Hi Emma / Kim — technical reply below, happy to cover live.

1) Execution locations: by default, customer workloads are pinned to the region chosen at provisioning. For Redwood Hosted, our model serving fleet has regional pools (EU, US, APAC). For this account we can enforce EU-only execution for inference requests.

2) Failover / burst: there are two mechanisms:
   - Configurable failover policy: customers can choose to disallow cross-region fallback in their routing policy (hard block).
   - Optional burst routing for capacity spikes: if enabled, burst will route to compatible model variants in other regions.

We recommend a contractual hard block for procurement if you require absolute EU execution — otherwise we will provide a documented notification & approval workflow for any planned cross-region activity.

3) KV cache / persistence: ephemeral KV cache used for attention caches is not written to persistent backups. Customer content persisted by the customer (e.g., user-uploaded artifacts) is stored per-region.

4) Logs & backups: operational logs used for debugging are retained in-region; logs containing customer content are redacted. Backups of persistent customer artifacts (S3-like) are stored in the provisioned region unless the customer opts into cross-region replication.

5) Encryption & key management: at-rest + in-transit encryption is standard. Customers on Redwood Private can bring their own KMS (BYOK); hosted customers may opt for CMK-style managed keys.

6) Subprocessors: our infra providers (cloud partners) are listed in our DPA; we can provide the subprocessor list and notify in advance of changes.

I've attached a clause-level matrix mapping to common procurement asks (dpa_clause_matrix.xlsx). For procurement language, suggested signable paragraph below:

"Redwood Inference confirms that, for the EU Hospitals Network account, Redwood will process customer data in the EU region(s) specified in the ordering document and will not route inference requests to non-EU infrastructure unless explicit prior written consent is provided by the customer or a pre-agreed emergency failover policy is invoked. Redwood will provide reasonable prior notification for any cross-region processing and will maintain appropriate technical and organizational measures (encryption at-rest/in-transit, access controls, and subprocessor controls) as described in the Redwood DPA and SCC mapping."

If that meets procurement needs we can convert to a short signable form.

-Dev
Platform Security Engineer
Attachments: dpa_clause_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)

- We need an explicit statement confirming whether transient model context (KV caches, prompt context) is ever replicated to US-based GPUs or persisted outside the EU for debugging or telemetry. You say ephemeral and not written to persistent backups; can you add a sentence that it is not replicated to non-EU regions for Hosted EU-pinned accounts?
- Please clarify whether anonymised/pseudonymised patient records could be included in any model fine-tuning or telemetry collection by Redwood teams.
- For the procurement packet we also require a short SCC mapping snippet that shows which standard clause numbers map to Redwood controls (or a link to the mapping).

Attached is our procurement checklist — feel free to populate the relevant fields. Can you get a signable statement and the SCC snippet by COB Thursday?

Regards,
Lars
